title: kestrel journal
description: Jo Halloran's journal, written mostly after shifts at the Blue Kestrel diner in Gridfall.

data.author: Jo Halloran
data.tagline: notes from the counter, mostly written at 3 in the afternoon
data.about:
I am Jo. I am thirty-one. I live on Fenn Avenue in Gridfall and I work the morning shift at the Blue Kestrel on Mill Street, which means I get up at 4:10 and I am useless by two. I started this because Marla said I should and because typing is quieter than talking.

I do not write about customers by name. If you think a post is about you it probably is not. If it is, I will take it down if you ask.

posts.title: first post, I guess
posts.body:
Marla has been telling me for four months that I should keep one of these. Her argument was that I tell the same three stories to the same people and that if I wrote them down I would notice and stop. That is not a compliment but she is not wrong.

So. This is a journal. I work at the Blue Kestrel on Mill Street in Gridfall. Morning shift, five to one, Tuesday through Saturday. Ed owns it. Ed has owned it since 1978 and he sits in the second booth from the door and does the ordering out of a spiral notebook that he will not let anybody else touch.

I have worked here two years and four months. Before that I did nine years at the fastener plant in Pell, in receiving, until they cut the second shift. People ask if I miss it. I miss the money. I do not miss standing in the same eleven square feet.

Things I am probably going to write about: the fryer, the Tuesday men, weather, whatever Ed says.

Things I am not going to write about: customers by name, my mother, the thing with the car.

Marla's page is over at [url=synth://marla.verity.net/]marla.verity.net[/url] if you want the version of all this with photographs and a better attitude.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: you did it. I am putting you on my links page tonight before you change your mind.

comments.author: Jo
comments.body: I have not changed my mind. I have however already deleted a paragraph.

comments.author: dennis o.
comments.body: Nine years in receiving at the fastener plant and you never once said hello to me in the yard. I was the one with the clipboard.

posts.title: twelve hours and the fryer
posts.body:
The fryer went down Thursday at 6:40 in the morning, which is the worst possible time because that is when the hash comes off it and the second wave comes in at seven.

Ed's position is that the fryer is fine and that the thermostat is a liar. Ed's position on most equipment is that it is fine and that some component of it is a liar. He has been right about this more often than he should be.

What we did: I ran the flat top for everything, Marla took the whole floor herself for two hours, and Ed stood behind the counter with a screwdriver and a paper towel and did something I did not watch.

[quote=Ed]It is not the element. If it was the element it would not come up at all. It comes up and it lies about where it is.[/quote]

He was right. It was the thermostat. The parts man in Ardo had one and Ed drove out for it himself at eleven and was back by twelve thirty and we never closed.

Twelve hours in the building, counting the drive. I got home and sat in the car in the driveway for a while, which is a thing I have started doing and have decided not to think about.

The thing nobody tells you about restaurant work is that it is not hard in the way you expect. It is hard in the way where you are standing and then you are still standing.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: two hours. I want the record to show it was two hours and forty minutes and the Tuesday men each wanted a separate check.

comments.author: H. Speltz
comments.body: The Ardo parts house is open until 5 and they will hold things if you call. Tell Ed. He will not listen but tell him.

posts.title: the fire people still come in
posts.body:
Six months since the substation and we still get the crews.

When it happened in June we were the only building on the block with a working stove because Ed has gas and the gas never went anywhere. We ran for four days on candles and a camp lantern and Ed would not take money from anybody in a uniform. That was his decision and he made it at about six in the morning on the first day and never discussed it.

So now there is a linemen's table. Not every day. Two or three mornings a week, four of them, coffee and whatever is fast, and they are gone by 6:30 because they stage out of the Quarry Road yard.

They do not talk about the fire in front of me anymore. In June they talked about nothing else. One of them told me the smell was the worst part and that it was not smoke, it was the oil, and that it got into his jacket so badly he threw the jacket away.

The town is still arguing about it. There is an entire thread over on [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]boards.gridfall.net[/url] that I read sometimes when I cannot sleep, and it has gotten to the point where people are posting scans of their electric bills at each other.

I do not have an opinion about the transformers. I have an opinion about the linemen, which is that they tip in cash and they stack their own plates.

comments.author: Carl B.
comments.body: You should have an opinion about the transformers. I live two hundred feet from them.

comments.author: Jo
comments.body: Carl you come in on Fridays and you have told me your opinion about the transformers. I have heard it. It is a good opinion. I am still not putting it on a website.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: the jacket thing gets me every time you tell it

posts.title: snow, and the Tuesday men
posts.body:
Nine inches Sunday night. Mill Street was not plowed until eight, and we opened at five anyway because Ed lives four blocks away and walks.

First hour: nobody. Second hour: the Tuesday men, all four of them, on a Monday, which has never happened.

The Tuesday men are retired county highway. They have had the back two booths since before I worked here and possibly since before Ed owned the place. They come Tuesdays. That is the arrangement. On Monday they came because it snowed and because three of them had spent thirty years plowing that exact street and could not sit at home while somebody else did it badly.

They watched out the window for two hours and provided commentary. Gale Mundt's crew got a review. It was not a rave.

[quote=one of the Tuesday men]He is carrying the wing too high on the second pass. He knows it. His father knew it too.[/quote]

They each left a dollar on a ninety cent coffee, which they have done for as long as I have known them, and which I am fairly sure they coordinated in 1991 and have never revisited.

I like the winter shifts. Nobody is in a hurry in the snow. In August people are in a hurry at 5:15 in the morning and I have never understood who they are hurrying for.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: you forgot the part where one of them tried to tell you how to run a plow route and you said you would pass it along to the county

comments.author: Jo
comments.body: I did pass it along. Gale comes in on Thursdays.

comments.author: g.mundt
comments.body: The wing was where it needed to be. There is a storm drain on that pass that has eaten two blades since 1998. Tell them that.

posts.title: a list of things people leave
posts.body:
Cleaned out the lost and found box because it would no longer close. Contents, complete, going back I think to 2001:

[list][*]Eleven pairs of reading glasses. Nine of them are the same drugstore pair.[*]Three single gloves, all left hand, none matching.[*]A house key on a keyring shaped like a fish.[*]A paperback with a library sticker from a library in another state.[*]Two hearing aid batteries, loose.[*]A photograph of a dog standing in front of the water tower.[*]A pay stub from the tannery, which closed in 1987, so somebody was carrying that around on purpose.[*]A hymnal.[*]Forty-one cents.[*]A note on a napkin that says only "tell her the answer is yes" and which I am not throwing away and will not read again.[/list]

Ed's rule is that we keep things a year. Ed's actual practice is that we keep things forever in a box under the register and nobody has ever asked for anything except the glasses.

I put the fish keyring on the corkboard by the door, where it will sit until the building falls down.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: the napkin has been in that box since before I started. I have read it probably forty times.

comments.author: dennis o.
comments.body: The tannery pay stub is probably Roy Purdy's. He kept one in his wallet and showed it to people. He passed in 2001.

comments.author: Jo
comments.body: Dennis that is either the saddest or the best thing anybody has put in these comments and I have been thinking about it for a day.

posts.title: Ed says the lease
posts.body:
Ed told me and Marla on Thursday after close, standing at the register, not sitting down, which is how I knew before he said anything.

The lease is up in September. Hollis Property in New Ardo owns the building. The number they want is not a number that works. He said it twice, the same way both times, like he had practiced it in the car.

I asked if there was anything to be done and he said he had spent three weeks on that question and the answer was no.

Marla asked if it was business and he got annoyed, which is rare, and said business is fine, business has been fine for twenty-six years, do not let anybody tell you the town stopped coming, because the town did not stop coming.

Then he went back to the notebook and did the ordering for next week like it was a normal Thursday, and we both stood there for a minute and then we did the side work.

I do not know what I am going to do. I am thirty-two in August. There is nothing on Mill Street. The fastener plant is not hiring and would not take me back into receiving anyway, and the only other place in the county that opens at five is the truck stop out on 62 and that is a forty minute drive at four in the morning in January.

I am not going to write about this every day. I am telling you once so that when the posts get strange you know why.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: I have not told anybody. I have wanted to tell everybody. Reading it here is worse somehow.

comments.author: H. Speltz
comments.body: The historical society has been trying to get somebody to care about that block for fifteen years. If there is anything at all I can do, ask.

comments.author: Carl B.
comments.body: Hollis Property also owns the two vacant storefronts by the crossing and has for six years. Make of that what you want. I have.

comments.author: Jo
comments.body: Carl please do not start a thread about this on the boards. Ed reads them. He will not say so but he does.

posts.title: six weeks
posts.body:
Six weeks and change. Ed set the date for August 22. He picked a Sunday because Sunday is the short shift and he said he did not want a long last day.

The word got out around the Fourth and now it is the only thing anybody says to me. Every single person, all day, five to one.

"I heard about the Kestrel." Yes. "What are you going to do?" I do not know. "This town is going to hell." It is not, it is going to New Ardo, which is worse.

I have gotten polite about it. Marla has not and I admire her for it. Tuesday she told a man who has been in maybe four times since I started that if he had come in once a month instead of once a year we would be having a different conversation, and then she apologized, and then at the end of the shift she said the apology was the part she regretted.

We are busier than we have been in three years. That is the joke of it. August will be our best month since 2001 and then there will be no September.

Somebody put the Kestrel on the county wiki at [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/]wiki.gridfall.net[/url]. It is mostly right. It says we opened in 1959. We opened in 1961. I am not going to be the one to fix it because I do not know how those pages work and because I do not want to look at it.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: I stand by all of it including the apology which I also stand by regretting

comments.author: d.carrow
comments.body: Anybody can fix the wiki, you just click edit. If you tell me the right year I will do it and put the Ledger piece in as the source. No charge, obviously.

comments.author: Jo
comments.body: 1961. It was Kestrel Creek Lunch until 1968. Ed has the original menu in a frame in the back and I looked at the date on it this morning specifically so I could answer you.

posts.title: last shift
posts.body:
We opened at five. There were nine people on the sidewalk at 4:50, which has never happened and which Ed pretended not to see.

We ran out of eggs at 9:40. Ed sent me to Hollis Market and they gave me eleven dozen and would not take the money, and I stood in that aisle and had to get myself together before I could walk out with the cartons.

We ran out of everything else by 11:20. Ed came out from behind the counter, which he does not do, and said we were closed, and somebody started clapping, and he put his hand up and it stopped immediately, which tells you something about Ed.

The Tuesday men came on a Sunday. All four. They sat in the back two booths and stayed until we put the chairs up.

Marla took photographs all morning. They are on her page now. I have not looked at them and I am not going to for a while.

At the end Ed did the register the way he does it every day, same order, and wrote the number in the spiral notebook, and then closed the notebook and put it in his coat instead of in the drawer, and that was the part that got me.

He said thank you to both of us. He said it once and he meant it and then he asked if we wanted the rest of the pie.

I took the pie. I am not going to pretend I did not take the pie.

The key is on the corkboard with the fish keyring. Not on purpose. I hung it there out of habit when I came in at 4:40 and nobody thought to take it down.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: photos are up. take your time. they will keep.

comments.author: H. Speltz
comments.body: I was one of the nine on the sidewalk. I want you to know the whole block was quiet at 4:50 in a way I have not heard since the fire.

comments.author: dennis o.
comments.body: Forty three years. My father ate there the week it opened under the old name. There is not going to be another one.

comments.author: Ilene K.
comments.body: My kids will not remember it and that is the thing I keep getting stuck on.

posts.title: temp work at the fastener plant
posts.body:
Ten weeks. The agency in Ardo put me at the Pell plant on second shift, packing, through the end of the year and "possibly beyond," which in agency language means no.

It is the same building I left in 2001. Different door. They repainted the lunch room and it is the same lunch room.

Second shift is two to ten thirty. I have not been awake at ten thirty at night on purpose since I was twenty-five. The first week I could not sleep and the second week I could not do anything else.

Nobody talks on the line, which after three years of five hundred conversations a morning is a thing I did not expect to mind.

Marla is at the Hollis Market deli counter now. She likes it more than she says she does. Ed has not answered his phone in six weeks and Marla went by the house and he was fine, he was just not answering the phone.

I drove Mill Street on Saturday because it is the way to the bank. The windows are papered. Somebody has put a sign in the corner of one that says WATCH THIS SPACE, and I do not know who put it there or when, and it has been there long enough that the tape has gone yellow.

That is all. I am going to try to sleep before two.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: I like it fine. the deli slicer is better than ours was. do not tell anybody I said that.

comments.author: d.carrow
comments.body: If the agency thing ends, the county is posting a part time clerk job in the spring. I will send you the notice when it goes up.

posts.title: I drove past
posts.body:
The sign is gone off the front of the building. Ed took it down himself in January with a rented lift and two men from the volunteer fire department, and it is in his garage on Fenn Avenue now, which I know because I live on Fenn Avenue and I watched them carry it in from my kitchen window.

It is eleven feet long. It does not fit anywhere. It is standing on edge against the back wall and his car is in the driveway now and will be in the driveway all winter.

I have not been inside the building since August. I do not think I am going to be.

The agency work ended December 22 as expected. I have been on unemployment since and doing Saturdays at the market with Marla when they need a second on the counter, which is not a job, it is a favor she arranged and I know it and she knows I know it.

There is snow on the roof of 214 Mill Street and nobody has raked it and that is the sort of thing that finishes a building.

I keep thinking I will write something here that is not about the diner. I sit down and it is about the diner.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: it is a job if I put you on the schedule and I am putting you on the schedule. come in thursday.

comments.author: H. Speltz
comments.body: If Ed ever wants that sign out of his garage the society has a wall for it. Tell him no rush and no strings. Tell him whenever.

comments.author: Carl B.
comments.body: Write about something else then. Write about the railroad. They are going to close that too and nobody is paying attention.

posts.title: not much
posts.body:
Started at the county clerk's office in April. Part time, twenty-four hours, filing and the front window. It is fine. The people are fine. I am up at seven instead of four ten and my back has stopped doing the thing it did.

I have started four posts since February and not finished any of them.

I think what this was, was a thing I did after a shift, and there is no shift now, and sitting down to write about the clerk's office at eight in the evening is not the same and I am not going to pretend it is.

So I am going to leave it here rather than let it go quiet on its own, which is what was going to happen anyway.

The archive stays up. Marla has the photographs at [url=synth://marla.verity.net/]marla.verity.net[/url] and she is better at this than I ever was. The county wiki page about the diner is correct now, including the year, which somebody fixed within about a day of me complaining about it, and I never properly said thank you for that.

If you came here from the ring at [url=synth://webring.gridfall.net/]webring.gridfall.net[/url], the next site along is worth your time.

Thank you for reading. It was twenty months and about eleven posts, which is not much, and it got me through a thing.

comments.author: marla
comments.body: you are not allowed to do this without telling me first. call me tomorrow.

comments.author: d.carrow
comments.body: It was me on the wiki. Took about four minutes. You already said thank you, in July, in a comment. I kept it.

comments.author: dennis o.
comments.body: Leave it up. In ten years this will be the only place anybody wrote down what that counter was like at six in the morning.

comments.author: Ilene K.
comments.body: My oldest asked me last week what used to be at 214 and I read her the last shift post. She is nine. She listened to all of it.
